title: Identifying cytokine signaling signatures in primary human Th-1 cells by phospho-proteomics analysis
protocol: Cut the lower tube of the bag containing the blood samples.
Introduce the cut tube properly in a 50 mL Falcon tube to avoid spillage of the blood.
Cut the upper tube after securing the blood sample in the Falcon tube.
Distribute 50 mL of blood between two clean, sterile 50 mL Falcon tubes (25 mL in each tube).
Add 25 mL of RPMI-1640 media without additives to each tube.
In 50 mL Falcon tubes, add 25 mL of sterile Lymphoprep.
Slowly layer 25 mL of 1:2 diluted blood on top of the Lymphoprep layer.
Use an electronic pipette controller with a 25 mL pipette.
Carefully place the tip of the 25 mL pipette containing 25 mL of blood in touch with the Lymphoprep layer and slowly add the blood on top.
Spin tubes at 800 g in a swing-bucket rotor centrifuge for 30 min at 18°C–25°C with maximum acceleration but no brake.
Collect the white buffy coat layer that forms an interface between the plasma layer above and the red blood cells below into a clean, sterile 50 mL Falcon tube using sterile pastettes.
Wash the cells with 50 ml RPMI-1640 without additives.
Centrifuge cells down at 300 g for 5 min with maximum acceleration and deceleration.
Repeat washing step.
Resuspend the pellet in 50 ml of RPMI-1640 supplemented with 100 Units/mL Penicillin, 100 μg/mL Streptomycin, and 2 mM L-Glutamine.
Count the number of cells in a Flow cytometer gating on the lymphocytes based on their forward scatter (FSC) and side scatter (SSC) profile.
Dilute 10 μL of the cell suspension in 490 μL RPMI to achieve a 1:50 dilution.
Count cells in the Flow cytometer for 60 s at a flow rate of 1 μL/s.
Calculate the total number of lymphocytes in the 50 mL sample using the number of lymphocytes counted and accounting for the 1:50 dilution factor.
Transfer 108 lymphocytes into a new 50 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL PBE buffer (sterile PBS supplemented with 0.5% BSA and 2 mM EDTA).
Collect cells again by centrifuging at 300 g for 5 min.
Resuspend the cells in 500 μL PBE buffer.
Transfer resuspended cells to a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Stain cells with 30 μL of anti-CD4-FiTC antibody at +4°C for 15 min.
Transfer 10 μL of stained cells into a 96 well V-bottom plate.
Spin down cells in the Falcon tube at 300 g for 5 min at +4°C.
Repeat the PBE wash to remove unbound antibody.
Resuspend the cells in 500 μL of PBE buffer and add 50 μL of anti-FiTC microbeads.
Incubate the cells at +4°C for 15 min.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL of PBE buffer and spin them down at 300 g for 5 min at +4°C.
Repeat step to remove excess unbound microbeads twice.
Equilibrate an LS column on a QuadroMACS separator with 3 mL of PBE.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL of PBE buffer.
Proceed to isolate CD4 stained cells using Magnetic Activated Cell Sorting with the equilibrated LS column and QuadroMACS separator.
Wash the column three times with 3 mL of PBE buffer after loading the cells.
Collect eluates from the three washes plus the flow-through sample.
Transfer 10 μL of the flow-through into a 96 well V-bottom plate to check isolation efficiency.
Remove the LS column containing CD4 stained cells and place it into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Add 5 mL of PBE buffer to the sample.
Flush out CD4 positive T cells by firmly applying the plunger supplied with the LS column.
Transfer 10 μL of the flow-through into a 96 well V-bottom plate.
Dilute samples in the 96 well plate by adding another 190 μL (1:20 dilution).
Count cells in a flow cytometer to check isolation efficiency and determine CD4+ T cell number.
Resuspend 10^7 CD4+ T cells in 5 mL of RPMI-1640 supplemented with Pen/Strep and L-Glutamine.
Activate CD4+ T cells for three days in the presence of 300 μL ImmunoCult Human CD3/CD28 T cell Activator and 20 ng/mL IL-2 under Th1 polarizing conditions (20 ng/mL IL-12, 10 ng/mL anti-IL-4).
Spin down cells at 300 g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL of light, medium, or heavy SILAC RPMI-1640 medium.
Supplement the medium with 20 ng/mL IL-2, 20 ng/mL IL-12, and 10 ng/mL anti-IL4.
Prepare amino acids stock solutions in newly opened, sterile PBS.
Store 0.5 mL aliquots of amino acid stock solution at -20°C.
Combine all reagents required for the preparation of SILAC media.
Filter the media using a 500 mL Stericup Filtration System.
Keep the filtered media at +4°C.
Count the number of cells every two to three days.
Dilute the cells down to 10^6 cells/mL if necessary.
Grow the cells in the appropriate SILAC medium supplemented with IL-2, IL-12, and anti-IL-4 for 5 cell division cycles.
Count cells in a flow cytometer and collect about 108 cells per SILAC labeling by centrifugation at 300 g for 5 min.
Transfer collected cells into a clean T175 flask containing 25 mL of the appropriate SILAC media without IL-2.
Starve the cells for 24 h in the SILAC media to reduce basal levels of signaling pathways engaged by cytokines.
Collect cells again by centrifugation after starvation.
Resuspend cells in SILAC RPMI-1640 media containing FBS.
Stimulate T cells grown in light SILAC media with no additional treatment as a reference control.
Stimulate T cells grown in medium SILAC media with 20 nM IL-6 for 15 min.
Treat T cells grown in heavy SILAC media with 2 μM of MSC2530818, a specific CDK8 inhibitor, for 30 min followed by stimulation with 20 nM IL-6 for 15 min.
Wash cells three times with 50 mL of ice cold PBS after stimulation.
Combine cells in a 1:1:1 ratio (light : medium : heavy).
Collect approximately 10^6 cells labeled with different amino acids (light, medium, and heavy).
Transfer the collected cells into clean, low protein binding microcentrifuge tubes.
Prepare SDS-containing lysis buffer by dissolving 1% w/v SDS in 100 mM TEAB pH8.
Incubate cell pellet (1 volume) in SDS-lysis buffer (5 volumes) on ice for 10 min to ensure complete cell lysis.
Centrifuge the cell lysates at 20,000 g for 15 min at +4°C.
Transfer supernatants from centrifuged samples to clean Falcon tubes.
Determine protein concentrations using a BCA Protein Assay kit.
Transfer 10 mg of total protein per experiment of combined light, medium, and heavy labeled proteins into a clean, low protein binding microcentrifuge tube.
Reduce the protein sample with 10 mM dithiothreitol for 1 hour at 55°C to break all disulfide bridges and linearize the proteins.
Alkylate the protein sample with 20 mM iodoacetamine for 30 min at 18°C–25°C.
Precipitate the proteins using six volumes of chilled (−20°C) acetone for 16 h at −20°C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 14,000 g for 30 min at +4°C to obtain protein pellets.
Resuspend protein pellet in 1 mL of 100 mM TEAB.
Add 50 μg of Trypsin to the resuspended proteins and incubate for 2 h.
Add another 50 μg of Trypsin and digest the protein for 16–24 h at 37°C with shaking at 1000 rpm.
Centrifuge the digested samples at 20,000 g for 30 min at +4°C to clear the samples.
Determine the peptide concentration using a Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay.
Lyophilize 3.5 mg of peptides per sample using an EZ-2 Plus Centrifugal Evaporator (GeneVac) with HPLC program settings for 40 h at 40°C.
Resuspend lyophilized peptide samples in 200 μL Buffer A.
Trap the resuspended samples on a XBridge trap cartridge.
Separate peptides using an Ultimate 3000 RSLCnano system with a gradient of Buffer A and Buffer B.
Collect 80 fractions of 0.8 mL each from 1 to 80 min over the chromatogram.
Concatenate fractions to provide 20 fractions based on online UV values at 200 nm.
Dry concatenated fractions using an EZ-2 Plus Centrifugal Evaporator prior to phosphopeptide enrichment.
Use 50 μL of MagResyn Ti-IMAC beads per sample.
Transfer 3 mL of MagResyn into a 2 mL clean low protein binding microcentrifuge tube.
Place tubes in a magnetic separator and remove the solution after 10–20 seconds.
Resuspend particles in 2 mL of loading buffer and allow equilibration for 1 minute.
Remove the loading buffer after placing tubes back in the magnetic separator for 10–20 seconds.
Repeat steps three more times with new loading buffer.
Distribute microparticles into 60 clean, low protein binding microcentrifuge tubes.
Place tubes in a magnetic separator and remove supernatant.
Resuspend each peptide fraction in 100 μL of loading buffer by vortexing for complete resuspension.
Centrifuge samples for 10 minutes at 15000 g to remove insoluble material.
Transfer the supernatant into microcentrifuge tubes containing MagResyn Ti-IMAC microparticles, resuspending by vortexing for 10 seconds.
Incubate the peptide – microparticles mixture for 20 min at 18°C–25°C with continuous mixing.
Mix the contents every 2–3 min during incubation.
Place the tube on the magnetic separator and allow 10–20 s for the magnetic beads to separate.
Remove and discard the supernatant.
Wash the microparticles with 100 μL of loading buffer for 2 min with gentle shaking.
Place the tubes again in the magnetic separator after washing, and remove the supernatant once the microparticles have cleared.
Wash the microparticles with 100 μL of Wash buffer 1 for 2 min with gentle shaking.
Remove the supernatant by placing the tubes back in the magnetic separator and allowing 10–20 s for the magnetic microparticles to clear.
Repeat steps using Wash buffer 1, discarding the supernatant after each wash.
Wash the microparticles for 2 min with 100 μL of Wash buffer 2.
Remove and discard the supernatant after placing tubes in the magnetic separator.
Resuspend the magnetic microparticles with 150 μL of Elution buffer.
Incubate for 10 min at 18°C–25°C to allow elution of phosphopeptides.
Ensure the microparticles remain in suspension by constant gentle agitation at 1000 rpm during elution.
Place the tubes in the magnetic separator for 10 seconds to allow microparticles to clear.
Transfer the supernatant (eluted phosphopeptides) to a clean 1.5 mL protein low binding microcentrifuge tube with 50 μL of formic acid 10%.
Repeat elution steps with another 150 μL of Elution buffer.
Place the tubes again in the magnetic separator and allow 20 seconds for microparticles to clear.
Pool the supernatant with previously eluted phosphopeptides, adding a further 50 μL of 10% formic acid for a total volume of 400 μL.
Vacuum dry the eluates using an EZ-2 Plus Centrifugal Evaporator (GeneVac) on HPLC program at 40°C for 40 hours.
Load phosphopeptide samples onto a C18 trap column for washing with 0.1% formic acid for 5 minutes.
Resolve phosphopeptides using a gradient of Buffer A and Buffer B: from 5% Buffer B to 35%, then to 98%, back to 2%, and finally stabilize at 2% Buffer B according to the specified timeline.
Trap phosphopeptides in an Acclaim PepMap 100 C18 column (100 μm x 2 cm).
Separate phosphopeptides on an Easy-Spray PepMap RSLC C18 column (75 μm x 50 cm).
Transfer phosphopeptides to a Q Exactive Plus Mass Spectrometer via an Easy-Spray source with temperature set at 50°C and a source voltage of 0.2 kV.

Identify peptides using a top 15 method consisting of full scans and MS searches between m/z 350 to 1600, with MS2 scans having a resolution of 70,000, max fill time of 20 ms, and set lock mass at 445.120024 for data-dependent acquisition mode.
Scan the Q Exactive Plus Mass Spectrometer in centroid mode.
Set the resolution to 15,000.
Configure the isolation window to 1.4 m/z.
Adjust the normalized collision energy to 27.
Set the max fill time to 100 ms.
Enable dynamic exclusion for 45 seconds.
Analyze .RAW files using MaxQuant software.
Utilize the Andromeda search engine within MaxQuant.
Configure Andromeda for the Uniprot Homo sapiens database (release date: 2018_09).
Set minimal peptide length to 5.
Consider only phosphopeptides quantified in at least two out of three replicates.
Determine p values using Student’s t test corrected with Benjamini–Hochberg procedure.
Conduct GO analysis using DAVID tools.
